device and, with the appropriate modem, the output can be transmitted on
a telephone line.

Whilst the sealed 12 volt rechargeable lead-acid accumulator should
power the system on continuous operation for a period of approximately four
weeks, in the event of the battery discharging to the point at which erroneous
readings are likely, ‘Battery Low' is displayed on the printer and the complete
system is immediately shut down.

The transducer design which the author assembled at Bristol, U.K., and
which was adopted for the Mid-Levels study (G.C.0. 1980) is shown in Figure
2.56 The tensiometers consist of a 22 mm external diameter, one bar air
entry porous ceramic cup glued to a cyclindrical perspex body of a similar
diameter. The manufacturers quoted transmission rate of water through the
cup wall is 5.3 ml hr ‘om 2 per 100 kPa of pressure difference across the
cup wall. A rubber bung through which a longer reading line and a shorter
de-airing return line pass, forms a seal at the upper end. The two lines
are made from twin polythene covered nylon tubing 267 mm I.D. and 4.7 mm O0.D.
The de-airing line can either be terminated at the ‘soil surface above the
tensiometer, or returned to a centrally located de-airing board housed with
the scanivalve and electronic enclosures.
